messages:
Maya Chen: Hi payroll team — my Feb 28 pay shows a 15% foreign tax credit withheld on my midyear bonus. Net is down ~SGD 1,200. I was still US tax resident that pay period. Can someone check payrun PR-2026-02-BONUS-472?

Devon (People Ops): Thanks Maya — assigning to Sam to investigate. Can you confirm the exact dates you were in SG vs US around Feb?

Maya Chen: I was physically in SG 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-14 for a short project, but my official tax residency didn’t change — US address and H1-B status active.

Sam (Payroll): Looking now. I can see PR-2026-02-BONUS-472 in the ledger. It shows a deduction labeled `SG_FTC:15%` applied at payroll step. Snippet from payrun:```
PR-2026-02-BONUS-472
employee: Maya Chen (EID 8421)
gross_bonus: SGD 8,000
deductions:
 - SG_FTC: 15% = SGD 1,200
net_paid: SGD 6,800
```
This was applied because the employee record flagged SG as primary residence on 2026-02-01 (HRIS sync).

Nadia (HRIS): I see the sync — there was an entry for a short assignment but `country_of_residence` remained US until 2026-03-15. However, a temporary location update (duration flagged >7 days) triggered a residency override in last nights sync. That override should have been gated — looks like a bug in the sync rule.

Devon (People Ops): OK — plan: Sam, please reverse the SG withholding and process a supplemental correction in the next payroll cycle so Maya receives the ~SGD 1,200. Also, we need to confirm tax reporting implications (W-2/other). Sam, loop in tax counsel if needed.

Sam (Payroll): Will do. Opening payroll ticket and scheduling reversal. Ticket PAY-12458 created. I'll process adjustment in next run and post an audit entry. Noting FX impact for finance. ETA reversal: next payroll (target date in system 2026-03-20). payroll-bot, please tag this with high priority.

payroll-bot: Ticket PAY-12458 created and tagged high priority. Notified Finance for FX reconciliation and Tax Counsel for reporting guidance. Estimated reversal run id: RR-2026-03-20-09. :gear:

Maya Chen: Thanks. Quick question — if SG withheld that 15%, will that create any need for a 1042-S or affect my W-2? I’m on H1-B and US tax resident for the period.

Sam (Payroll): Short answer: 1042-S is for nonresident alien withholding — you should not get a 1042-S. For US reporting (W-2) we report gross wages in USD; the reversal will adjust year-to-date wages. If the SG tax was actually remitted, we may pursue a refund or credit at source; we’ll also document for your 2026 tax prep (Form 1116 may apply if you end up claiming foreign taxes paid). I’ll confirm with tax counsel and update the ticket.

Devon (People Ops): Thanks everyone. Nadia — can you patch the HRIS sync rule to prevent temporary location updates from flipping `country_of_residence` automatically? Mark as P0 bug and add to release.

Nadia (HRIS): On it — creating infra ticket HRIS-7892, will revert the override and add a guard.

Sam (Payroll): Closing loop here — PAY-12458 will include reversal, supplemental pay stub, and an internal memo for tax. I’ll comment in the ticket when the reversal posts. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Appreciate it — please ping me when the supplemental payslip is posted so I can confirm net.

Devon (People Ops): Will follow up once payroll confirms. Thanks for reporting, Maya.
